amendments.rule: Rules 53 and 63 decide a verbless clause's supplied copula by what is left to carry it, and two configurations they do not name are settled in the corpus. Where the clause expresses **no subject at all** and the ASV supplies a subject pronoun along with the copula, rule 63's noun-phrase exception is switched off — no subject token stands for it to apply to — and the predicate carries both: `κοινωνὸς` → *he is partner*, `ἀπόστολοι` → *they are the messengers* and `δόξα` → *they are the glory* at 2CO.8.23, as `εὐπρόσδεκτος` → *it is acceptable*, `κρεῖσσον` → *it is better*, `καλὸν` → *it is good* and `ἀσφαλές` → *it is safe* do, and as `ἰδιώτης` → *I be rude* does for a Greek noun the ASV renders by a bare adjective. Discontinuity is not a reservation about this: `ἔξεστίν` → *it is lawful* and `γνώσει` → *am I … in knowledge* keep the supplied words with the predicate across intervening tokens under rule 15. Where the clause **does** express a subject and that subject is **not a lexical noun**, it falls on rule 53's pronoun side and takes the copula itself. A **substantival demonstrative** is the ordinary case: `αὕτη ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη` → *This is the first resurrection* and `τοῦτο … τρίτον` → *This is now the third time* give *This is* to the demonstrative, as `οἱ τοιοῦτοι ψευδαπόστολοι` → *such men are false apostles* gives *such men are* to `τοιοῦτοι` and leaves *false apostles* to the noun. Rule 63's *noun* means a lexical noun, and a demonstrative is no more one here than `ὑμεῖς` is. A **substantival quantifier or adjective** is no more one either and is decided the same way: `πάντα ὑμῶν` → *all are yours* gives *all are* to `πάντα`, headed on *all* under rule 17, and a bare *yours* to the genitive, exactly as the same frame gives *ye are* to `ὑμεῖς` at 1CO.3.23 while `Χριστὸς … θεοῦ` in that verse's second clause sends *is God's* to the predicate under rule 63, its subject being a lexical noun. A **predicate genitive** the ASV renders by an English possessive — *yours*, *Christ's*, *God's* — is a nominal predicate for rule 53's exception and is none of the prepositional, adjectival or adverbial predicates rule 53's main principle names, so it does not draw the copula to itself unless the subject is a lexical noun. An **attributive** demonstrative is the contrast, and rule 38's test tells them apart: it is part of the subject noun phrase rather than the subject itself, so `Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί` → *These words are faithful and true* leaves it a bare *These* and gives *are faithful* to the predicate adjective under rule 53. Rule 56 is untouched, since it speaks of a clause with no predicate at all.
amendments.why: 1CO.3.22 and 1CO.3.23 write the identical verbless predicate-genitive frame and were analysed two ways: the pass cited rule 63 for `πάντα ὑμῶν` because `πάντα` is not a pronoun, though rule 68 already says rule 63's *noun* means a lexical noun. The rule as written names only the substantival demonstrative, so the general test has to be inferred, and that inference is what the verse pass got wrong. The amendment names the test itself and adds the class this chapter met, and it also fixes what rule 68 nowhere says: that a predicate genitive rendered by an English possessive is a nominal predicate rather than one of rule 53's prepositional, adjectival or adverbial ones. No corpus row is disturbed — `Χριστοῦ` → *is Christ's* at COL.2.17 and the other predicate-genitive units all carry lexical-noun subjects and stay exactly where they are.

conventions: Supplied copula in a verbless clause whose predicate is a genitive the ASV renders by an English possessive: the subject's class decides, and only a lexical noun sends the copula to the predicate. 3:22 `πάντα ὑμῶν` → *all are* on the quantifier and a bare *yours* on `ὑμῶν`; 3:23 `ὑμεῖς … Χριστοῦ` → *ye are* on the pronoun and a bare *Christ's*; 3:23's second clause `Χριστὸς … θεοῦ` has the lexical-noun subject, so rule 63 holds and *is God's* goes to the predicate.

Rule 67 leaves the head of a complex frame open where the carrier is a proper preposition; this chapter takes it on the prepositional word. `κατὰ ἄνθρωπον` → *after the manner of* heads on *after* at 3:3, matching the bare `κατά` → *according to* on *according* at 3:8 and 3:10. A head on *manner* remains defensible in the corpus.

report: Read all 40 candidate groups and the dump end to end. Almost everything the table flags is context-licensed: the article's T→V bucket splits on rule 31 against rule 32 (3.7 s011 `ὁ αὐξάνων θεός` governs an expressed head noun, while 3.7 s003/s008, 3.11 s008 and 3.19 s014 are substantival); the T→A bucket splits on rule 47 displacement at 3.8 against a plain determiner at 3.19 and 3.20; `ἐποικοδομέω` keeps *thereon* inside the verb at 3.10 and 3.14 and drops it at 3.12 only because `ἐπί` is expressed there (rule 106); `εἰμί` differs only by expressed-versus-supplied copula and by ASV word order; `ἕκαστος`, `τις`, `μηδείς` and `οὐδείς` all head on the quantifier with *man* or *one* as generic completion; `κατά` heads on the prepositional word at 3.3, 3.8 and 3.10 alike.

One real split, and the lemma table cannot show it because both sides are `aligned`. 1CO.3.22 and 1CO.3.23 are the same verbless frame — a nominal subject, a predicate genitive the ASV renders by an English possessive, and a supplied copula — and they put the copula on opposite sides. 3.23 gives *ye are* to the pronoun subject `ὑμεῖς` under rule 53's noun-phrase-predicate exception; 3.22 gave *are yours* to the predicate `ὑμῶν` citing rule 63, although its subject `πάντα` is a substantival quantifier and not the lexical noun that rule 68 says rule 63's *noun* means. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, so 3.22 is patched: *all are* to `πάντα` headed on *all*, a bare *yours* to `ὑμῶν`.

3.23 is correct as it stands and is not patched: its second clause has the lexical-noun subject `Χριστός`, so rule 63 properly sends *is God's* to the predicate, and 3.21 has an expressed `ἐστιν`, so no placement question arises there.

Checked the `added`-versus-fold axis separately, the table being keyed by source lemma and blind to it. The chapter marks `added` only where no token licenses the English (3.2 *to bear it*, licensed by nothing; 3.4 the resumed copula *am*, `εἰμι` already spent on t006) and folds a repeated function word onto the member it introduces (3.2 *with* on `βρῶμα`, 3.3 *not* on `περιπατεῖτε`, 3.16 *that* on `οἰκεῖ`). Those are rule 103's own two arms, so the two treatments are not a split. 3.17's supplied *and* is folded onto `οἵτινες`, the token carrying the clause linkage under rule 86's test, and the unit's note already concedes `added`.

BSB disagreements: all six are documented convention differences and none is an error. 3.7 ὁ is rule 31 (the article governs the expressed `θεός` and the ASV writes it no determiner); 3.8 τὸν twice is rule 47 (`ἴδιον` carries *his own*); 3.13 τὸ and 3.15 τὸ are rule 20 (*each man's*, *any man's* occupy the determiner slot); 3.19 τῷ is rule 23. Nothing was changed for them.

The note repeated at 3.10, 3.16 and 3.17 — an article before a name with no English determiner — is a direct application of rule 23 and is deliberately not logged as a convention; the contract already binds it in every verse.
